mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 0.5% signals accommodative monetary policy that compresses discount rates, directly increasing equity valuations and producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS remains below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 6.0% signals labor market weakness that triggers central bank rate cuts, boosting equity valuations and producing positive S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE exceeds 6.0%.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous declines in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicate broad demand contraction, causing recession fears that drive negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline in prior month
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO < 105.0) signals manufacturing slowdowns that reduce corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 105.0.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts falling below 1700.0 thousand units signal housing market weakness that reduces consumer confidence and drives negative S&P 500 returns within 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when HOUST < 1700.0.

mechanism_narrative: High inflation (CPIAUCSL > 265.0) combined with rising rates (FEDFUNDS > 0.5%) signals aggressive monetary tightening that reduces equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 265.0 and FEDFUNDS > 0.5.

mechanism_narrative: Non-farm payroll growth exceeding 140,000 thousand persons indicates labor market strength that increases consumer spending and drives positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS exceeds 140,000.

mechanism_narrative: Retail sales exceeding 620,000 million dollars signal strong consumer demand that supports corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of instances when RSAFS > 620000.0.
